sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Explicitly confirmed to have no impact on channel folding, trafficking, or function (L12, PMC7988323); surface expression confirmed by antibody staining in multiple studies.
sites.rationale: Six independent publications pin the myc-tag junction to exactly E146|Q147 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology 144–154). Python confirms residue 146 = E and residue 147 = Q. The insert sits 3 residues from the TM1 C-terminus (143) and 8 residues from the TM2 N-terminus (155), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-clearance rule. L12 explicitly states the modification has no impact on folding, trafficking, or function, placing this at the highest validation tier. Full-length human KCNQ1 expressed in mammalian cells with a c-Myc epitope (EQKLISEEDL) inserted between Glu146 and Gln147 in the extracellular S1–S2 linker; construct used to quantify plasma-membrane surface abundance by antibody staining. Multiple independent groups (PMC7988323, 2020.07.29.227231, PMC5842040, PMC12632771, PMC13041670, PMC12724399) report the identical junction.

sources.claim: The c-myc tag (EQKLISEEDL) was inserted into the extracellular S1–S2 linker between residues Glu146 and Gln147.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by Alexa 647 fluorescence via flow cytometry (L11, PMC5764571). Electrophysiological function not explicitly reported as preserved in the ledger clips.
sites.rationale: Three independent publications pin the BBS-tag junction to exactly Y148|A149 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology 144–154). Python confirms residue 148 = Y and residue 149 = A. The insert sits 5 residues from the TM1 C-terminus (143) and 6 residues from the TM2 N-terminus (155), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-clearance rule. The BBS peptide (13 aa) falls within the 13–23 aa target range. Surface display is confirmed by flow cytometry; channel function is not explicitly reported as preserved in the available ledger clips, so validation is surface_only. Full-length KCNQ1 expressed in mammalian cells with a 13-residue bungarotoxin-binding site (BBS) peptide inserted between residues 148 and 149 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop; construct (BBS-Q1-YFP) used for surface labeling with fluorescent α-bungarotoxin. Reported independently in PMC11429900, PMC12218124, and PMC5764571.

sources.claim: A 13-residue bungarotoxin binding site peptide (BBS) sequence was introduced between sequences for residues 148 and 149 in KCNQ1 extracellular S1–S2 loop using QuikChange Lightning Site-Directed Mutagenesis kit (Stratagene) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)
ordered surface loop (12 aa): pLDDT>=70, DSSP loop/turn, exposed junction residue (max RSA), indel-tolerant, 3D-clear of features

literature_notes: All thirteen ledger lines converge on two junctions in the same extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology 144–154): E146|Q147 (myc tag, L1–L7, L12–L13) and Y148|A149 (BBS 13 aa, L8–L11). No other extracellular loops in KCNQ1 are addressed by any ledger line. The S3–S4 linker (216–220, only 5 residues) and the S5–pore–S6 region (283–327) have no ledger support and are not proposed. The intracellular N-terminus (1–122) and the large intracellular C-terminus (344–676) are not extracellular and are excluded. L4 and L5 also mention mEGFP fused to the C-terminus (intracellular, residue 676), but a C-terminal tag on KCNQ1 is cytoplasmic and therefore not a surface-tag site; it is not listed in other_positions because no ledger line reports it as a tolerated intracellular tag in isolation — it is always co-present with the extracellular myc tag.
